findings.desc: Test coverage does not load-bear the authority_job_create provider CLI schema change. The implementation changed command-catalog provider from z.enum([codex, claude-code, gemini]) to z.string().min(1), but the added tests only call submitAuthorityJobFromPlan directly with custom provider strings and inspect signed envelopes. No command catalog or CLI surface smoke asserts that authority_job_create.provider is string/min(1) or invokes the command with a custom provider, so a regression back to the enum would still let the direct submitter tests pass while the actual CLI/tool argument boundary rejects custom provider declarations.

packages/main/src/core/authority-client.ts:1546-1550 only rejects provider === fake after calling normalizeAuthorityRunnerProvider. That normalizer lowercases only known aliases/canonical codex/gemini but preserves unknown raw values (authority-mode.ts:420-426), and the command schema now accepts any non-empty provider string (command-catalog.ts:2227). As a result, authority_job_create --provider Fake or FAKE is treated as a custom non-fake declaration and can be signed/submitted even though the job-create path promises a non-fake provider declaration. Fix by rejecting the reserved fake provider case-insensitively (for example, check raw.trim().toLowerCase().replace(/_/g, -) === fake) before preserving custom provider spelling.
